subject: Pilot streaming workload debrief & token-bucket profile
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Chen <emma@windward.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 22 Aug 2027 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot streaming workload debrief & token-bucket profile

Hi Emma — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap while it’s fresh so we can align next steps and sizing inputs.

Summary of what I heard from your team:
- Product: live guided-chat flows embedded in Windward Insights. Responses are typically 2–4 turns per session, with occasional longer context (user + system history) up to ~1,200 tokens.
- Latency SLOs: target 95th %ile user-perceived latency <= 150ms for streaming first-token + smooth token cadence (your engineering lead emphasized user experience during incremental output).
- Throughput: baseline steady QPS ~25 requests/sec during business hours, with predictable bursts (10x) for reporting windows and event-driven summaries — peak windows expected for 3–8 minutes, once or twice per day.
- Token mix: short-turn bursts (avg 80 tokens/resp) account for ~70% of traffic; long replies (~700–1,200 tokens) are ~5% but drive peak token/sec consumption.
- Concurrency: concurrent live sessions ~180 steady, peaks up to ~1.6k concurrent for special events.

Questions / clarifications we need to size for Dedicated or Hosted: 
1) Confirmed peak window length and cadence (you said ~5–8 mins; please confirm frequency).
2) Do you require strict streaming p95 for first token (hand-off to client) AND per-token cadence guarantees? If the former only, we can use chunked streaming optimizations; if the latter, we’ll stage different instance classes.
3) Any SLOs for downtimes or fallback model quality vs latency tradeoffs for degraded mode?

Attachments: I’ve attached two files — a small sample token export from your prod traces (windward_token_samples.csv) and our lightweight sizing template (redwood-sizing-template.xlsx). Please confirm the sample is representative.

Next steps I propose:
- Marissa and I will run the token sample through our batching simulator to produce tokens/sec curves and recommended pool sizing (GPU classes + quantization tradeoffs). ETA: 48 hours after you confirm sample representativeness.
- Internal sync (Redwood): Marissa + Lauren to align on concurrency slots and autoscaling policy recommendation for the pilot.
- Follow-up call: 30-min technical sync to review sizing outputs and an initial pilot run plan.

If that all looks right, Emma, can you confirm: (a) peak window frequency, (b) whether per-token cadence is a hard SLO, and (c) any compliance constraints for the pilot?

Thanks — Diego
Diego Fernandez
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
---
Attachments: windward_token_samples.csv (CSV, 75 KB), redwood-sizing-template.xlsx (XLSX, 120 KB)
From: Emma Chen <emma@windward.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot streaming workload debrief & token-bucket profile

Diego — thanks for the clear recap. A few answers inline: 

> peak window length and cadence
We see ~5–8 minute peaks during scheduled reports (twice/day at 09:00 & 17:00 PT) and the occasional event spike (marketing pushes) that last up to 20 minutes but are less frequent (1–2x/week).

> streaming p95 for first token vs per-token cadence
We need both. First-token p95 <= 150ms is non-negotiable for UX; per-token cadence should not drop below ~30ms/token on average for long responses (so output feels smooth). If tradeoffs are necessary, quality fallback is fine but we need a visible degradation mode that we can detect.

> downtimes / fallback
Yes — we need a fallback mode that prefers shorter summaries and optionally a lower-parameter model when capacity constrained. That’s acceptable if we can quantify quality loss.

Compliance: pilot data is not regulated, but procurement wants standard SOC2 assurances and audit logs for any dedicated environment.

We reviewed the sample file briefly — it looks representative but I’ll confirm with engineering by EOD.

Emma
Emma Chen
Head of Product, Windward Analytics
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emma Chen <emma@windward.ai>
Date: Tue, 24 Aug 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot streaming workload debrief & token-bucket profile

Looping you in with the sizing plan I want to run once Emma confirms sample. Quick internal notes / assumptions before we simulate: 

Assumptions to validate (internal):
- Effective avg tokens/sec per request during peaks (we’ll derive from samples) — initial guess: 18–24k tokens/sec across fleet during short bursts if long responses align with their 5% distribution.
- Streaming-first-token path needs a low-latency front layer (we should reserve a small pool of high-clock-rate A100s or equivalent), plus a separate pool optimized for long-token throughput (quantized on T4s/RTX6000-style capacity).
- Autoscaler policy: aggressive horizontal scaling for short spikes (target scale-up within 60s), warm standby for long-response slots to avoid KV cache cold starts.

Action items (internal):
- I’ll run the token samples through the batching/kv-simulator and produce two candidate configurations: Hosted pilot (cost-optimized) and Dedicated pilot (capacity/SLA-focused). Deliverable: tokens/sec heatmap + recommended GPU mix + expected p95 latencies per class. ETA: 48 hours after sample confirmation.
- Lauren: please prep an SRE note on fallback behavior and trace hooks to measure per-token cadence so we can quantify degradation.

I’ll push a draft sizing doc to the drive link once ready.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Chen <emma@windward.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Aug 2027 10:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot streaming workload debrief & token-bucket profile

Emma — great, appreciate the clarifications. Two quick scheduling items:

1) Please send confirmation on the sample file by EOD — Marissa and I will start the simulation the moment we get the green light.
2) Proposed follow-up: Thursday 26 Aug, 11:00 AM PT — 30-min technical review. I’ve created a HubSpot calendar invite and included the Drive link in the metadata (see also: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/WD-2027-058).

Initial acceptance criteria for pilot sizing we'll present: 
- Achieve p95 first-token <= 150ms for the majority (>=95%) of sessions in the pilot window.
- Maintain per-token cadence >= 30ms/token on long responses for >=90% of long-response requests.
- Provide fallback policy matrix (quality vs latency tradeoffs) and expected cost delta between Hosted and Dedicated options.

If that works I’ll lock the invite; otherwise propose a different time.

Thanks — Diego
